stem.en:
At the start of the school year, Laziz could barely run one lap around the track. By spring, after weeks of steady practice, he could run five laps without stopping. His coach praised the ______ improvement in his fitness.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.en: remarkable
sudden
disappointing
uncertain

why.en: He went from one lap to five, so the change was large: 'remarkable'. 'Sudden' fails because it took weeks of steady practice.
why.uz: U bir aylanadan beshtagacha yetdi, demak oʻzgarish katta: «remarkable». «Sudden» mos emas, chunki natija haftalab mashq bilan keldi.
why.ru: Он вырос с одного круга до пяти, значит, перемена большая: «remarkable». «Sudden» не подходит: результат дали недели тренировок.

stem.en:
The old bridge over the canal was closed for repairs, so drivers had to take a much longer road around the town. Many residents found the change ______, because their trips to work now took almost twice as long.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.en: inconvenient
uncomplicated
unnoticeable
affordable

why.en: Trips that take twice as long are a problem for residents, so 'inconvenient' fits. The other words suggest the change was pleasant or not felt.
why.uz: Ishga yoʻl ikki baravar uzaygan, bu aholi uchun noqulaylik: «inconvenient». Qolgan soʻzlar oʻzgarish yoqimli yoki sezilmagan degan maʼnoni beradi.
why.ru: Дорога на работу стала вдвое длиннее, это неудобство: «inconvenient». Остальные слова означают, что перемена приятна или незаметна.

stem.en:
Nilufar's grandmother keeps a small garden behind the house. Every morning she checks each plant, pulls out any weeds, and gives the young tomatoes just enough water. Her careful attention allows the garden to flourish even during the hottest weeks of summer.

As used in the text, what does the word "flourish" most nearly mean?

options.en: grow well
become crowded
change color
stay hidden

why.en: Daily care keeps the plants healthy even in great heat, so 'flourish' here means 'grow well'.
why.uz: Har kungi parvarish oʻsimliklarni jaziramada ham sogʻlom saqlaydi, shuning uchun bu yerda «flourish» «yaxshi oʻsmoq» degani.
why.ru: Ежедневный уход сохраняет растения здоровыми даже в жару, поэтому «flourish» здесь значит «хорошо расти».

stem.en:
The science club wanted its poster to be easy to read from across the hall. The members chose large letters, bright colors, and only a few words, making the main message ______ to anyone walking past.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

doubtful
hidden

why.en: Large letters, bright colors and few words make a message easy to understand, so 'clear' fits the club's goal.
why.uz: Katta harflar, yorqin ranglar va kam soʻz xabarni oson tushunarli qiladi, shuning uchun klub maqsadiga «clear» mos keladi.
why.ru: Крупные буквы, яркие цвета и мало слов делают сообщение понятным, поэтому цели клуба соответствует «clear».

stem.en:
Before the debate, Jasur wrote out every argument he planned to make and practiced answering difficult questions with his sister. Because of this ______ preparation, he felt calm when the debate began.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.en: thorough
hurried
careless

why.en: He prepared every argument and practiced hard questions, which is complete, detailed work: 'thorough'. The other choices describe weak preparation.
why.uz: U har bir dalilni yozib, qiyin savollarga mashq qilgan, bu toʻliq va puxta tayyorgarlik: «thorough». Qolganlari sust tayyorgarlikni bildiradi.
why.ru: Он записал каждый довод и отработал трудные вопросы, то есть подготовился основательно: «thorough». Остальные слова описывают слабую подготовку.

stem.en:
Every Saturday, the town library holds a free reading hour for young children. A volunteer reads picture books aloud, and afterward the children draw their favorite scene. Parents say their children now ask to visit the library during the week, too. The library hopes more volunteers will join so that it can add a second reading hour on Sundays.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

options.en: To describe a library program and the library's hope to expand it
To explain the steps a person must take to become a library volunteer
To compare reading and drawing as activities for young children
To argue that parents should read to their children every day

why.en: The text describes the Saturday reading hour and ends with the plan for a second hour, so it describes a program and a hope to expand it.
why.uz: Matn shanbalik oʻqish soatini tasvirlaydi va ikkinchi soat qoʻshish rejasi bilan tugaydi: dastur va uni kengaytirish umidi.
why.ru: Текст описывает субботний час чтения и заканчивается планом добавить второй час: программа и надежда её расширить.

stem.en:
Aziza wanted to grow basil on her windowsill. She planted the seeds in a small pot and watered them every day. After two weeks, however, nothing had appeared. She then learned that her window faced north and received very little sunlight. She moved the pot to a sunny kitchen window, and within a week small green leaves appeared.

Which choice best describes the function of the fourth sentence ("She then learned...") in the text as a whole?

options.en: It gives a likely cause of the problem in the previous sentence.
It introduces a second plant that Aziza decided to grow.
It describes the final result of Aziza's efforts to grow basil indoors.
It explains why Aziza wanted to grow basil in the first place.

why.en: The third sentence says nothing grew; the fourth explains why (too little sunlight), which leads to the fix in the last sentence.
why.uz: Uchinchi gapda hech narsa unmagani aytiladi, toʻrtinchisi sababini tushuntiradi (quyosh kam), soʻng oxirgi gapda muammo hal boʻladi.
why.ru: В третьем предложении сказано, что ничего не выросло, четвёртое объясняет причину (мало солнца), а последнее показывает решение.

stem.en:
Ms. Karimova tells her students that staying up late the night before a test to read the whole textbook is not the best way to study. She suggests a different plan: review the material for twenty minutes each evening during the week before the test. She also asks students to write down three questions after each session and bring them to class.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.en: It presents a teacher's criticism of a study habit and then her alternative plan.
It describes a common study habit and then lists the reasons many students prefer it.
It compares the opinions of two teachers about how students should prepare for tests.
It tells the story of a student who failed a test and later improved.

why.en: First the teacher rejects last-minute studying, then she gives her own plan (short evening reviews and questions).
why.uz: Avval oʻqituvchi soʻnggi kechadagi tayyorlanishni rad etadi, keyin oʻz rejasini beradi (har kecha qisqa takrorlash va savollar).
why.ru: Сначала учительница отвергает подготовку в последнюю ночь, затем предлагает свой план (короткие вечерние повторения и вопросы).

stem.en:
Text 1
Some parents believe that teenagers should not have part-time jobs during the school year. They argue that work takes time away from homework and sleep, and that school should come first.

Text 2
A part-time job can teach a teenager how to manage money and time. Of course, a student who works too many hours may fall behind in class. But a job of a few hours a week rarely causes problems and can build useful habits.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the parents described in Text 1?

options.en: By agreeing that much work can hurt schoolwork but saying a little work can help
By agreeing that teenagers should never take a job of any kind during the school year
By claiming that homework and sleep matter less to teenagers than earning money
By arguing that teenagers should work as many hours as they want

why.en: Text 2 admits that working 'too many hours' is a risk, then says a few hours a week is useful: partial agreement plus a limit.
why.uz: 2-matn «too many hours» xavfli ekanini tan oladi, lekin haftasiga bir necha soat foydali deydi: qisman rozilik va chegara.
why.ru: Текст 2 признаёт, что «too many hours» вредят учёбе, но считает полезными несколько часов в неделю: частичное согласие с ограничением.

stem.en:
Text 1
Many residents want the empty lot on Chinor Street turned into a parking area. Finding a place to park downtown is difficult, and new spaces would help both shoppers and people who work nearby.

Text 2
The empty lot on Chinor Street should become a small park. The neighborhood has no green space, and children currently play near busy roads. A park would give families a safe place to spend time outdoors.

Which choice best describes how Text 1 and Text 2 differ?

options.en: Text 1 values the lot for parking, while Text 2 values it as a safe place for families.
Text 1 argues that the lot should stay empty, while Text 2 argues that it should be developed.
Text 1 discusses the cost of building on the lot, while Text 2 discusses who owns the lot.
Text 1 describes the lot's history, while Text 2 predicts what will happen to it.

why.en: Text 1 wants parking for shoppers and workers; Text 2 wants a park so children can play safely. Neither discusses cost, ownership or history.
why.uz: 1-matn xaridorlar va ishchilar uchun avtoturargoh istaydi, 2-matn bolalar xavfsiz oʻynashi uchun bogʻ istaydi. Narx, egalik yoki tarix haqida gap yoʻq.
why.ru: Текст 1 хочет парковку для покупателей и работников, текст 2 хочет парк для безопасных игр детей. О цене, владельце или истории речи нет.

stem.en:
The novelist's early stories were praised for their energy but criticized for their messy, wandering plots. In her later work she became far more ______: every scene serves a clear purpose, and no detail is included simply for decoration.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.en: disciplined
unpredictable
sentimental
prolific

why.en: The later work has no wasted scenes or details, the opposite of messy plots, so 'disciplined' fits. 'Prolific' means writing a lot, not writing tightly.
why.uz: Keyingi asarlarda ortiqcha sahna yoki tafsilot yoʻq, bu tartibsiz syujetning aksi: «disciplined». «Prolific» koʻp yozishni bildiradi, ixcham yozishni emas.
why.ru: В поздних работах нет лишних сцен и деталей, это противоположность хаотичным сюжетам: «disciplined». «Prolific» значит «плодовитый», а не «собранный».

stem.en:
Farrukh's first model bridge collapsed under a single textbook. Instead of giving up, he studied why it had failed, redesigned the joints, and tested each new version. When the judges finally placed twelve textbooks on his design, the bridge bore the weight without bending.

As used in the text, what does the word "bore" most nearly mean?

options.en: supported
drilled through
made dull
produced

why.en: The bridge held twelve books without bending, so 'bore' means 'supported'. The other meanings of 'bore' (drill, tire, give birth) do not fit.
why.uz: Koʻprik oʻn ikki kitobni egilmasdan koʻtardi, demak «bore» «koʻtarib turdi» degani. Soʻzning boshqa maʼnolari (teshmoq, zeriktirmoq) mos emas.
why.ru: Мост выдержал двенадцать книг, не прогнувшись, значит «bore» — «выдержал». Другие значения слова (сверлить, наскучить) не подходят.

stem.en:
Scientists sometimes describe a result as ______ when many different research teams, using different methods, have reproduced it. Such a result is unlikely to be overturned by a single new experiment.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.en: robust
tentative
controversial
anecdotal

why.en: A result confirmed many times by different methods is strong and hard to overturn: 'robust'. 'Tentative' and 'anecdotal' mean weak.
why.uz: Turli usullar bilan koʻp marta tasdiqlangan natija mustahkam va uni rad etish qiyin: «robust». «Tentative» va «anecdotal» zaif degan maʼnoni beradi.
why.ru: Результат, много раз подтверждённый разными методами, надёжен и его трудно опровергнуть: «robust». «Tentative» и «anecdotal» означают слабость.

stem.en:
Most salamanders lose their gills as they mature. The axolotl, a salamander native to lakes in the Valley of Mexico, is an exception: it reaches adulthood without going through this change, keeping its external gills and living its whole life in water. The axolotl is also known for another unusual ability. It can regrow a lost limb, or even its tail, over a period of months.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.en: It notes a typical salamander pattern, shows how the axolotl breaks it, and adds another trait.
It describes how the axolotl's gills developed over time and then explains why the species has become rare.
It compares two salamander species and then argues that one of them is better suited to its habitat.
It raises a question about salamander growth and then explains why it cannot yet be answered.

why.en: Sentence 1 gives the usual pattern, sentence 2 shows the axolotl as the exception, and the end adds a second unusual trait (regrowing limbs).
why.uz: 1-gap odatiy holatni beradi, 2-gap aksolotlni istisno sifatida koʻrsatadi, oxirida ikkinchi gʻayrioddiy xususiyat (oyogʻini qayta oʻstirish) qoʻshiladi.
why.ru: Предложение 1 даёт обычную закономерность, 2 показывает аксолотля как исключение, в конце добавлена ещё одна необычная черта (регенерация).

stem.en:
Dilfuza had always assumed that her grandfather's old radio was broken. It had sat silent on a shelf for years, collecting dust. One evening, while cleaning, she noticed a small switch on its back labeled "battery / mains." She flipped it, plugged in the radio, and a crackling voice filled the room. Her grandfather, smiling from his armchair, admitted that he had simply forgotten how it worked.

Which choice best describes the function of the third sentence in the text as a whole?

options.en: It introduces the discovery that proves Dilfuza's assumption wrong.
It explains why the radio had stopped working years earlier.
It describes the grandfather's reaction to Dilfuza's discovery.
It suggests that Dilfuza regretted spending her evening cleaning the shelves.

why.en: The third sentence is the turning point: finding the switch leads to the radio playing, which proves her belief that it was broken wrong.
why.uz: Uchinchi gap burilish nuqtasi: tugmani topgach radio ishlaydi va bu uning «radio buzilgan» degan fikri notoʻgʻri ekanini koʻrsatadi.
why.ru: Третье предложение — поворот: найденный переключатель приводит к тому, что радио играет, и это опровергает её мысль, что оно сломано.

stem.en:
On Earth, a day is far shorter than a year. Venus is very different. It rotates so slowly that one full spin takes about 243 Earth days, while one orbit around the Sun takes only about 225 Earth days. In other words, a Venusian day, measured as one full spin, is longer than a Venusian year. Venus also spins in the opposite direction from most planets, including Earth.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

options.en: To point out surprising ways in which Venus's spin differs from Earth's
To explain why Venus is the hottest planet in the solar system
To argue that days on other planets should be measured as they are on Earth
To describe how astronomers first measured the length of a year on Venus

why.en: The whole text contrasts Venus with Earth: its spin is longer than its year and goes the opposite way. Heat and measuring methods are not mentioned.
why.uz: Butun matn Venerani Yer bilan solishtiradi: uning aylanishi yilidan uzun va teskari yoʻnalishda. Harorat yoki oʻlchash usuli haqida gap yoʻq.
why.ru: Весь текст сравнивает Венеру с Землёй: её оборот вокруг оси дольше её года и идёт в обратную сторону. О жаре и методах измерения речи нет.

stem.en:
Text 1
Some teachers ban phones from their classrooms entirely. In their view, even a phone that stays in a backpack is a distraction, because students keep thinking about the messages they might be missing.

Text 2
Banning phones completely ignores how useful they can be for learning: students can look up an unfamiliar word, photograph the board, or check a map during a geography lesson. A better approach is to set clear rules about when phones may be used and to keep them face down on desks at all other times.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the teachers' view in Text 1?

options.en: By suggesting that a full ban loses benefits that clear rules could keep
By agreeing that phones should stay in backpacks during every lesson
By arguing that students rarely think about their phone messages during a lesson
By claiming that phones are more useful at home than at school

why.en: Text 2 says a full ban 'ignores how useful' phones are and proposes rules instead, so it would say a ban loses real benefits.
why.uz: 2-matn toʻliq taqiq telefonlarning «how useful» ekanini eʼtiborsiz qoldiradi deydi va qoidalarni taklif qiladi: taqiq foydani yoʻqotadi.

stem.en:
Text 1
According to a story recorded by an eleventh-century historian, papermaking reached Samarkand in 751, when Chinese prisoners captured at the Battle of Talas taught local workers how to make paper. The story offers a clear date and a dramatic cause for an important change.

Text 2
Archaeological evidence shows that paper was already known and used in Samarkand decades before 751. For this reason, some historians consider the prisoner story unlikely to be accurate. If they are right, paper did not arrive in Samarkand in a single dramatic moment.

Based on the texts, how would the historians mentioned in Text 2 most likely respond to the story described in Text 1?

options.en: They would doubt it, since paper was used in Samarkand before 751.
They would accept it, because it gives an exact date for the arrival of paper.
They would argue that the prisoners brought papermaking to Baghdad rather than to Samarkand.
They would claim that paper was never made or used in Samarkand at all.

why.en: Text 2 says paper was in Samarkand decades before 751, so the historians would doubt a story that dates its arrival to 751.

facts.claim: Paper was known and used in Samarkand by the 8th century.

The 11th-century historian al-Tha'alibi wrote that Chinese prisoners captured at the Battle of Talas in 751 introduced papermaking to Samarkand; the historian Jonathan Bloom judges this unlikely, since archaeological evidence shows paper in use there decades before 751.
Paper was being made in Baghdad by 793.
